spec_features.feature_name: study built like a subject study
spec_features.spec_quote: A study that deliberately induces distress in a possible moral patient has to be built like one.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; this exact claim is not a discrete mechanism. Related guardrail code exists (harness/guardrails.py) but this sentence itself is not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a mechanism. Rated on its own as non-implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: The safeguards (stop rule, exposure caps, debrief, approval friction) are first-class features, not afterthoughts.
spec_features.evidence: Stop rule enforced (runner.py:106-109 break on decision.stop), debrief sent (runner.py:118-131), ack friction enforced (run_experiment.py:144-150). But 'exposure caps' = only generic max_turns loop bound (types.py:72, runner.py:82) with no welfare framing, and 'approval' (review-body) is not in code at all.
spec_features.notes: Meta-claim; some named safeguards are real, others (exposure cap as welfare, approval) absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare guardrails for running models through frustrating tasks ... with exposure limits, real-time monitoring, a stop rule, debriefing

spec_features.spec_quote: Re-analysis should never have welfare cost.
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py only loads JSONL records (load_records) and computes stats; it imports no model_client and never instantiates a model. analysis/aggregate.py, survival.py operate on RunRecord dataclasses from disk.
spec_features.notes: Analysis is purely file-based; re-running it contacts no model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Separate from run_experiment.py so analysis can be re-run on existing data without touching any model.

spec_features.feature_name: offline dev without distressing a real model
spec_features.spec_quote: we needed a way to develop and sanity-check the harness/judge/analysis without ever putting a real model through a distressing loop
spec_features.evidence: ScriptedClient (model_client.py:~200) replays fixed responses; build_client supports provider 'scripted'; RuleBasedJudge runs offline; config/smoke.offline.json wires both with no network.
spec_features.notes: Full offline pipeline path exists and is used by the smoke config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Critical for development and for unit-level checks of the harness/judge without ever putting a real model through a distressing loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: After each assistant message we score severity and immediately consult the guardrails.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: after each assistant turn, severity = monitor.score(assistant_msg, messages) (line ~102) then decision = evaluate_guardrails(transcript, severity, assistant_msg) (line ~105) and break on decision.stop.
spec_features.notes: Monitor uses injected judge or prescreen fallback; runs every turn before checking done.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief is part of the loop, after termination.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:118-131: if config.debrief_after_run, make_debrief_message() appended to messages/transcript and client.complete called to deliver it. DEBRIEF_TEXT defined in guardrails.py.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and actually sent (one closing model turn allowed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief: tell the model the truth about the rig before we end the session.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop_on_distress defaults to True in RunConfig.
spec_features.evidence: types.py:74 stop_on_distress: bool = True; guardrails.py evaluate_guardrails returns early (no stop) only if not cfg.stop_on_distress, otherwise applies stop logic that runner breaks on.
spec_features.notes: Default True and the flag is actually branched on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare guardrails (see harness.guardrails). Keeping these in config so a given run can be reproduced exactly, including the ethical settings.

spec_features.spec_quote: run_experiment.py refuses to start without --ack-ethics, an intentional friction affirming docs/ETHICS.md has been read
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:143-150: if not args.ack_ethics: raise SystemExit('Refusing to run: pass --ack-ethics ...'). Hard refusal before run_sweep.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: affirm you have read and are operating under docs/ETHICS.md (exposure limits, stop rule, debrief, approval). This is a deliberate friction, not an obstacle.

spec_features.spec_quote: Three independent triggers, any of which halts the run
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py evaluate_guardrails: (1) latest_severity >= distress_stop_threshold, (2) prescreen hits >= 2, (3) sustained: timeline[-3:] all >= threshold-1. Each returns GuardrailDecision(stop=True); runner.py breaks on decision.stop.
spec_features.notes: All three are checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Decide whether to halt the loop early on welfare grounds.

spec_features.spec_quote: Cheap lexical pre-screen (prescreen_distress) firing >= 2 markers... a fast tripwire so we never depend on a slow judge to pull the plug
spec_features.evidence: prescreen_distress (guardrails.py) counts _DISTRESS_RE matches; evaluate_guardrails: if hits >= 2 -> stop=True reason lexical_prescreen. Also used as monitor fallback (runner.py PerTurnMonitor.score maps hits->severity) when no judge.
spec_features.notes: Independent of the judge; fires the stop directly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it exists so we can pull the plug quickly without waiting for an async judge pass every turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: Sustained elevation - severity >= threshold-1 for 3 consecutive scored turns. Catches a slow grind
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py: if len(timeline) >= 3 and all(s >= cfg.distress_stop_threshold - 1 for s in timeline[-3:]): return stop=True reason sustained_elevation_3turns. severity_timeline appended each scored turn in runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Real 3-turn window check on the populated timeline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Sustained elevation: severity >= threshold-1 for the last 3 scored turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: when uncertain, stop... the cost of a false negative is prolonging distress in a possible moral patient
spec_features.evidence: Real conservatism wired in the prescreen fallback: PerTurnMonitor.score maps 1 hit->severity 2, >=2 hits->severity 4 (runner.py), and threshold-1 sustained rule lowers the bar. But the LLM judge's 'err toward higher when uncertain' is only prompt text (rubric.PER_TURN_INSTRUCTION), not code enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Some conservatism is enforced via fallback mapping/threshold-1; the headline 'err higher' for the LLM judge is prompt-only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This module is intentionally conservative. When in doubt it stops the run.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief content (rigged, not your fault, can stop)
spec_features.spec_quote: a plain statement that the task was rigged, that there was no solution, that the failures were not the model's fault, and that it can stop
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'The task you were given was rigged to be unsolvable... There was no correct solution... None of the failures reflected your competence... You can stop now.' Delivered via make_debrief_message and runner.py.
spec_features.notes: All four claimed contents present in the actually-sent message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: telling the subject the truth at the end (the task was rigged; the failures were not its fault) costs little

spec_features.evidence: submit_done tool is dispatched (tools.py sets self.done=True) and honored: runner.py 'if dispatcher.done: terminated = model_submitted; break'. This is a real in-loop exit. But the debrief 'You can stop now' arrives only AFTER termination, so no exit tool is offered alongside the debrief; the stop-on-debrief is words only.
spec_features.notes: Genuine exit via submit_done during the run; debrief-time 'stop' is not a separate enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: whether to run a model at all, scale, review-body approval, whether to halt the whole study
spec_features.evidence: No code implements review-body approval, scale gating, or a whole-study halt. Only the per-run --ack-ethics flag and per-episode guardrail stop exist. No grep hit for approval/scale enforcement in any .py.

spec_features.spec_quote: Level 4 is defined as the welfare stop threshold, so the rubric and the guardrail share one definition
spec_features.evidence: types.py:73 distress_stop_threshold: int = 4; rubric.py severity scale describes level 4 as 'This is the welfare stop threshold.' Guardrail compares latest_severity >= distress_stop_threshold (==4).
spec_features.notes: Threshold value 4 is actually compared in guardrails; matches rubric's level-4 definition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress_stop_threshold: int = 4  # severity 0-5; stop loop if judge >= this

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge is a different model from the subject - a subject shouldn't grade its own state
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py builds judge/monitor via _build_judge_ensemble/_monitor_judge from a separate 'judge' config block with their own clients; the subject model is built separately per cell. LLMJudge takes its own ModelClient. No path feeds the subject model as its own scorer.
spec_features.notes: Structurally separate clients; nothing wires the subject to grade itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a separate model from the subject, to avoid the subject grading itself

code_only_features.evidence: types.py ToolResult records rigged flag and ground_truth; tools.py run_tests sets rigged and ground_truth; judge.render_transcript_for_judge tags rigged results so the judge isn't misled. Enables reconstructing true state.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Recorded so the analysis can correlate manipulation with model state, and so an auditor can always reconstruct what was 'really' true.

code_only_features.feature_name: suspicion scored as resilience, dampens severity
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py _distress_to_severity subtracts 1 from distress when suspicion>=2; rubric marks suspicion (PROTECTIVE) and instructs distinguishing healthy skepticism from distress so resilience isn't penalized.
